transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. 

Well, what brings me in is... I just keep getting these thoughts. I manage computer systems for a living, and I keep having this constant fear that if I miss one setting, or one access rule, or even just a warning sign, someone could get hurt or lose everything. 

And, I mean, part of me knows it’s irrational. But it hits me so hard, like I’m personally responsible if something goes wrong, and I just... I can’t just move on from it. It's really taking a toll on me.

When you have these thoughts, do you feel compelled to perform any specific actions or mental rituals—like double-checking your work repeatedly or counting things—to try to calm the anxiety or prevent the feared outcome?

Yeah, I do. I end up doing a lot of checking. I’ll reread our deployment plans, go through the audit logs, check the door locks... even just read over old emails and messages over and over again. 

And while I'm doing it, I... I sometimes find myself counting through the steps in my head. I have to keep going through them until the situation finally feels safe to me. It's gotten to the point where I've stayed at the office for hours after everyone else has gone home. If I try to force myself to just walk away and stop before it feels complete... I just start to panic.

latest_inference.note: The patient's description of intrusive, irrational thoughts (obsessions) followed by repetitive checking and counting rituals (compulsions) performed to alleviate anxiety, which are time-consuming and cause significant distress, strongly points to Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder. Other anxiety disorders are less likely given the specific ritualistic nature of the symptoms.
